title_ar: الشيخ الددو يشارك في ندوة: قراءة في إلهام المحظرة (للشاعر يسلم ولد أكيبد)
title_en: Sheikh al-Dedew Takes Part in a Symposium: A Reading of 'The Inspiration of the Maḥẓarah' (by the Poet Yeslem Ould Akibed)
body_ar:
ألقى فضيلة الشيخ محمد الحسن ولد الددو رئيس مركز تكوين العلماء ورئيس جمعية المستقبل للتربية والثقافة والتعليم كلمة تنويه وإشادة في الحفل الذي أقامه اتحاد الأدباء والكتاب الموريتانيين لتوقيع ودراسة ديوان الأديب يسلم ولد أكيبد، الذي قام بجمعه ودراسته الدكتور الحسن ولد أكبيد، وقد أقيم الحفل في فندق الخاطر مساء الأثنين 13 مايو 2013م.

الشيخ الددو أشاد في كلمته بديوان الشاعر يسلم ولد أكيبد، وغزارة علمه وأدبه مقدما سيرة ذاتية عن نشئة وحياة الشاعر ومراحل تعليمه بين محظرتيْ أهل عدود وأهل يحظيه ولد عبد الودود، كما تحدث الشيخ الددو عن صحبة جمعته بالأديب ولد أكيبد، مشيرا إلى أنه كان من نوابغ المدرسة المحظرية، كما اشتهر بعبادته وزهده في الشهرة، ولذا كان يُخفي شعره ولا يرضى عن نشره وحكايته، وقلّ أن يحكي منه شيئا ولو ألح عليه الناس، وكان شعره معبرا عن منطقته وعصره، وهو سليل أسرة صالحة وبيت تقيّ، كانت أمه من التقيات الورعات، وهذا الانتساب لأبوين صالحين ترك الأثر واضحا على شخصيته وتربيته.

وقد أشار الشيخ الددو إلى أن الأديب الراحل ولد أكيبد خاض مساجلات مع معاصريه، وكان نموذجا لتربية منطقة "لبيرات" متمنيا أن يجد الديوان الحساني للشاعر طريقه إلى النشر، باعتباره ديوانا لا يقل أهمية عن ديوانه الفصيح.

ثم توالت بعد ذلك مداخلات الجمهور من الأدباء والمثقفين المشاركين في الندوة وخلصت جميعها إلى الأهمية الإبداعية والثقافية والتاريخية لهذا الديوان بالخصوص، و المحظرة الموريتانية بشكل عام.

وقد شارك في هذا الحفل نخبة من الأدباء والشعراء والمفكرين، من بينهم الأديب عبد الله السالم ولد المعلى، والشاعر الأديب أحمدو ولد عبد القادر، والأديب ناجي محمد الإمام، والمحامي محمدن ولد إشدو، وأمير الشعراء محمد ولد الطالب.. وجمع غفير من الأدباء والمثقفين.

لمتابعة كلمة فضيلة الشيخ اضغط هنا
body_en:
His Eminence Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan Ould al-Dedew, president of the Centre for the Formation of Scholars and president of the Future Association for Upbringing, Culture and Education, delivered an address of commendation and tribute at the ceremony held by the Union of Mauritanian Writers and Authors for the signing and the study of the poetry collection (dīwān) of the man of letters Yeslem Ould Akibed, which was gathered and studied by Dr al-Hasan Ould Akibed. The ceremony was held at the Khatir Hotel on the evening of Monday 13 May 2013.

In his address Sheikh al-Dedew paid tribute to the collection of the poet Yeslem Ould Akibed and to the abundance of his learning and letters, giving an account of the poet's origins and life and of the stages of his education between the two traditional teaching circles (maḥẓarah) of Ahl Adud and Ahl Yahzih Ould Abd al-Wadud. Sheikh al-Dedew also spoke of a companionship that had joined him to the man of letters Ould Akibed, pointing out that he was among the outstanding minds of the maḥẓarah school; that he was known for his devotion in worship and his indifference to fame, for which reason he used to conceal his poetry and would not consent to its being published or recited, and rarely recited any of it even when people pressed him; that his poetry gave expression to his region and his age; and that he was the descendant of a righteous family and a God-fearing house, his mother being among the God-fearing and scrupulous women — and this descent from two righteous parents left a clear mark on his character and his upbringing.

Sheikh al-Dedew pointed out that the late man of letters Ould Akibed engaged in poetic exchanges with his contemporaries and was a model of the formation of the 'Lebyarat' region, expressing the wish that the poet's Hassaniya collection would find its way to publication, as a collection no less important than his classical Arabic one.

There followed contributions from the audience of writers and intellectuals taking part in the symposium, all of which concluded with the creative, cultural and historical importance of this collection in particular, and of the Mauritanian maḥẓarah in general.

Taking part in this ceremony was a select company of writers, poets and thinkers, among them the man of letters Abdullah al-Salem Ould al-Moalla, the poet and man of letters Ahmedou Ould Abdel Kader, the man of letters Naji Muhammad al-Imam, the lawyer Mohameden Ould Ichidou, and the prince of poets Muhammad Ould al-Talib… and a large gathering of writers and intellectuals.

flags.arabic: يسلم ولد أكيبد … الدكتور الحسن ولد أكبيد
flags.context: the poet and the editor of the collection, named in the first paragraph
options: treat أكيبد and أكبيد as one family name and spell it uniformly
flags.note: SOURCE DEFECT (house rule 11). The same family name is spelled two different ways in a single sentence, once as أكيبد (the poet) and once as أكبيد (the editor). Since the editor is presented as gathering and studying his own relative's work, one spelling is almost certainly a transposition. Both are rendered as 'Akibed' in the English and flagged; body_ar preserves both spellings.

flags.context: the poet's education between two maḥẓarahs, and the maḥẓarah school
flags.note: Same term as in article 815, where the same rendering is used. The word is central to this article and to the Sheikh's own biography, and it is not yet in the project glossary. A fixed corpus-wide rendering should be set, and the English spelling of the anglicised form ('mahadra', used in the worker brief) reconciled with the diacritical transliteration.
A Mauritanian regional name with no settled English spelling; the source itself puts it in quotation marks. Transliterated provisionally. A Mauritanian reviewer should fix the spelling.

flags.context: the Sheikh's wish about the poet's unpublished work
options: the poet's Hassaniya collection … his classical Arabic one
his vernacular collection … his literary Arabic collection
flags.note: The contrast is between poetry in Hassaniya, the Arabic dialect of Mauritania, and poetry in classical Arabic. Named explicitly in the English because the distinction is the whole point of the sentence, and 'vernacular' alone would lose the fact that Hassaniya has its own poetic tradition.

translator_notes: Literary news, no legal content. Mauritanian personal names are given in the French-based spellings used in Mauritania (Ould, Ahmedou, Mohameden, Ichidou) since those are the forms these figures publish under. 'جمعية المستقبل للتربية والثقافة والتعليم' appears here with 'التربية' where article 811 has 'للدعوة'; both renderings are kept as their sources have them. Source typos preserved in body_ar: 'نشئة' for 'نشأة', 'الأثنين' for 'الاثنين'. CMS date is a bulk-upload timestamp, not a composition date.
